new_entities.name: CPAP for mild obstructive sleep apnea
aliases: continuous positive airway pressure for mild OSA
CPAP in mild obstructive sleep apnea
new_entities.description: Continuous positive airway pressure treatment used in adults with mild obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Quality of life
new_entities.description: Health-related quality of life or sleep-related functional status measured with generic or disease-specific instruments.

edges.effect_quant: Mild-OSA trials are inconsistent for quality-of-life benefit: one 42-patient crossover RCT and one 31-patient sham-controlled crossover RCT found no clear QoL gain beyond placebo or sham, while a 142-patient randomized trial saw symptom and FOSQ improvement trends that did not reach significance.
edges.population: adults with mild obstructive sleep apnea, generally without severe daytime sleepiness
edges.mechanism: CPAP can reduce upper-airway obstruction and sleep disruption, but in mild OSA the symptom burden may be low enough that placebo effects and adherence limitations blunt quality-of-life gains.
edges.summary: For mild OSA, CPAP is far less convincing for quality-of-life improvement than it is for severe disease or for sleepiness relief. The overall signal is mixed and often dominated by placebo or sham responses.
edges.caveats: These trials are small, adherence is modest, and enrolled patients were often only mildly symptomatic. Individual patients with prominent symptoms may still benefit even when average trial effects are limited.

evidence.citation: BarnesM et al 2002 Am J Respir Crit Care Med
evidence.notes: A randomized controlled trial of continuous positive airway pressure in mild obstructive sleep apnea. No benefit over placebo in SF-36 or Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire measures.
Randomised controlled crossover trial of humidified continuous positive airway pressure in mild obstructive sleep apnoea. Quality of life was not improved more than sham CPAP.

evidence.citation: MonasterioC et al 2001 Am J Respir Crit Care Med
evidence.notes: Effectiveness of continuous positive airway pressure in mild sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome. FOSQ improved more in the CPAP group but did not reach significance.
